clue.text: Rifle a city

definitions.meaning: a make of repeating rifle, the lever-action gun of the American West
a cathedral city in Hampshire, England, once the capital of Wessex

explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a famous American firearm and to an old English cathedral city.

clue.text: Which person comes to a stop?

parts.note: the question word asking which person is 'who'

explanation.surface: A riddle asking who it is that arrives at a halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop' is the command shouted to a horse to make it halt; 'comes to' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The call to a horse to halt is an interjection meaning 'halt there'.

clue.text: Steal in prison

definitions.meaning: British slang for to pinch or pilfer
British slang for a police station or jail

explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses the one word both for pinching something and for the jail where you end up.

clue.text: No high-flying steeplechaser's occupation

parts.note: a jumping horse clears fences; a pilot who flies very low skims over the field boundaries in the same way

explanation.surface: A remark that a jump-racing horse's job involves no lofty flying.
explanation.walkthrough: Low-level flying that skims just over the field boundaries is named after what a steeplechaser does at each fence.
explanation.definitionFit: Flying very low over the countryside is like a jumping horse clearing obstacles, with no high altitude involved.

clue.text: The strength of new wines

indicators.note: something new has been remade, so the letters of wines are given a fresh order

explanation.surface: A remark on how strong a new vintage is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' looks like an adjective for the wine but rearranges the letters of 'wines'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tendons stand figuratively for muscular power, as in 'the sinews of war'.

clue.text: Repairing this shoulder-piece makes us tee up late

indicators.note: repairing puts something back together, so the letters of tee up late are reassembled

explanation.surface: Mending this shoulder decoration makes us late for our golf tee-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' points at the answer; 'Repairing' rearranges the nine letters of 'tee up late'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornamental strap on the shoulder of a uniform jacket is a shoulder-piece.

clue.text: Insect used to be quiet

parts.note: past tense of 'is': was
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: An insect that once kept quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: A stinging yellow-and-black flier is a kind of insect.

clue.text: Expressing regret for record in a poetic context

indicators.note: in with 'context' around it means the record word sits inside the surrounding words a poetic

parts.note: a log is a written record, such as a ship's log

explanation.surface: Saying sorry for a written record set in verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts LOG inside A POETIC; 'for' and 'context' just link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sorry and saying so is what an apology does.

clue.text: The rate at which centre page is misplaced

indicators.note: letters that are misplaced are put in the wrong positions, so centre page is rearranged

explanation.surface: How often the middle page of a newspaper goes astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is misplaced' rearranges the letters of 'centre page'.
explanation.definitionFit: A proportion expressed out of a hundred is a rate.

clue.text: "Bull'", said one toothy Westerner

indicators.note: said signals that the pieces are spoken, so their sound stands for the written word

parts.note: a bull is an ox, the word said aloud here
I is the Roman numeral for one
dental means to do with teeth

explanation.surface: A man with big teeth from the West introduces himself as a bull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' works on the word for a bull: OX spoken sounds like OCC, then I and DENTAL follow as written.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from the West, as opposed to an oriental, is so called.

clue.text: Brooke's urban type "squat and packed with guile"

definitions.text: Brooke's urban type "squat and packed with guile"

parts.words: Brooke's urban type "squat and packed with guile"
parts.note: Rupert Brooke's poem The Old Vicarage, Grantchester mocks the people of a nearby university town as 'urban, squat, and packed with guile'

explanation.surface: A quotation from Rupert Brooke describing a sly city dweller.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Old Vicarage, Grantchester the poet Rupert Brooke wrote that the people of the nearby university town 'rarely smile, being urban, squat, and packed with guile'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Cambridge, the town Brooke mocked, takes its Latin-derived name.

clue.text: Don't draw water — you might make things worse

definitions.text: Don't draw water — you might make things worse

parts.words: Don't draw water — you might make things worse
parts.note: advice not to disturb a water source, read as the idiom for not interfering with something that is fine

explanation.surface: Advice not to draw from a spring lest you spoil things.
explanation.walkthrough: Literally, leave the water source untouched; idiomatically, do not meddle with something that is working.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom advises not interfering with a satisfactory situation for fear of spoiling it.

clue.text: Gilbert's Major General knew "the — names of beings animalculous"

definitions.text: Gilbert's Major General knew "the — names of beings animalculous"

parts.words: Gilbert's Major General knew "the — names of beings animalculous"
parts.note: fill the gap in a line of the Major-General's patter song from Gilbert and Sullivan's The Pirates of Penzance

explanation.surface: A quiz on a line from Gilbert's comic song about a learned Major-General.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Pirates of Penzance, Major-General Stanley sings 'I know the ___ names of beings animalculous'; the blank is the missing word.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin taxonomic labels for tiny creatures are the names used by biologists in science.

clue.text: Cutting off abuse about a particle

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the abuse word goes around a

parts.note: an insult is verbal abuse
an ion is a charged particle

explanation.surface: Ending abuse concerning a tiny particle.
explanation.definitionFit: Lagging or shielding something isolates it, cutting it off from heat or electricity.

clue.text: Suitable letter

definitions.meaning: any letter other than a vowel

explanation.definitionFit: The word means 'in agreement or fitting' and also names a non-vowel letter.

clue.text: Heed a military order

definitions.meaning: the parade-ground command to stand up straight

explanation.definitionFit: The word means careful notice and is also the drill command shouted to troops.

clue.text: Taking article a short distance

parts.note: 'the' is the definite article
FT is the abbreviation for foot, a short measure of length

explanation.surface: Picking up a newspaper story from a little way off.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealing is the taking of property that is not yours.

clue.text: Provide oriental with clever repartee

parts.note: E stands for east, the oriental quarter
a quip is a witty remark

explanation.surface: Supplying an Easterner with sharp comebacks.
explanation.definitionFit: To fit out or furnish someone with what they need is to provide.

clue.text: Increasing by 200% - invest a thousand, in fear

indicators.note: to invest is to surround, so the thousand is put inside the tripling word

parts.note: adding 200% makes something three times as big: trebling
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Tripling one's money after investing a thousand pounds, but nervous about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invest' in its old military sense of besieging means surrounding; the 'investment' surface hides it.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaking from fright means being in fear.

clue.text: Naval academy in Spain, right? Wrong!

indicators.note: wrong means not as it should be, so the letters of in Spain right are set in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a naval college is in Spain and is told no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong!' rearranges the twelve letters of 'in Spain right'.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel used to teach cadets seamanship serves as a floating naval academy.

clue.text: Investment is up for instance a point

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is is read from bottom to top

parts.note: E is east, a compass point

explanation.surface: A remark that an investment has risen, for example by a point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Investment' is the old military sense of surrounding a town, not money; 'up' turns IS to SI.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest a fortress is to surround it, so investment is a military blockade.

clue.text: A bird's crop

definitions.meaning: A traditional name for a parrot
to cut short hair, horns or treetops

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a pet name for a parrot and also means to cut back.

clue.text: Chap in circulation

definitions.meaning: a man's name, short for Edward

explanation.definitionFit: It is a man's first name and also a small whirlpool where water circulates.

clue.text: Just bright and beautiful

explanation.definitionFit: The word means equitable, sunny and lovely in turn.

clue.text: Bread and butter turning bad I have introduced to Robin

indicators.note: introduced means put inside, so I have goes into the turned word
turning means the word for bad is read backwards

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill will
I've is the contraction of I have
Robin Hood, the outlaw of English legend

explanation.surface: A staple food going off, which I have brought to someone called Robin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses the word for bad to LLI; 'introduced' puts the contraction inside it, and 'to Robin' tacks on the outlaw's surname. Bread and butter is the idiom, not food.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread and butter is an idiom for one's basic income or means of living.

clue.text: Heel lacks ability

definitions.meaning: to heel over is to tilt or lean, as a ship does

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a tilt or slope, and with an apostrophe means 'is unable'.

clue.text: One after another, we hear, join on the inside

indicators.note: we hear tells the solver the pieces are spoken, so their sound stands for the written word

parts.note: in turn means one after another, the phrase said aloud here
to ally is to join together

explanation.surface: Taking turns to join something, as we are told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' works on IN TURN, which spoken sounds like INTERN; the joining word follows as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done within, rather than outside, happens on the inside.
